tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the loop-factory repo. Edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls, no skills — tests fixture-only, the Telegram sender is an injected argv template and is FAKED in tests. Factory code names no departments.

OWNED FILES (only these; all new):
  factory/triage_agent.py
  templates/systemd/loop-factory-triage.service
  templates/systemd/loop-factory-triage.timer
  tests/test_triage_agent.py

CONTEXT — owner directive (Ankit, 2026-08-02, verbatim intent): raw escalation rows were bombarding his Telegram; he wants 'a self-heal agent whose job it is to understand the goals and address the fixes through Ringer', with humans receiving only what genuinely needs them. Existing machinery to READ and reuse (do not modify): factory/selfheal.py (the propose-only L0-L5 ladder: next_rung, propose_patch, build_dossier — your classification should feed it), factory/charter_loader.py (goals live in charters: setpoints.objectives, thresholds), departments/*/state/decisions_outbox.jsonl + state/decisions_outbox.jsonl (escalation row shape: {kind:'escalation', department, issue, context, ts, eli5}), /home/ankit114/.config/loop-factory/outbox_push.yaml (the ping argv pattern — your config mirrors its senders.ping shape).

BUILD factory/triage_agent.py — the deterministic escalation-triage consumer:
1. CLI: --repo-root, --config <yaml>, --execute (default DRY RUN printing a JSON plan), --now (ISO, for tests). Config shape: {outboxes: [paths], ping: [argv template with {text}], max_pings_per_run: 1, digest_cooldown_hours: 6}.
2. CURSOR: own state at <repo-root>/state/triage/cursor.json mapping outbox path -> byte offset. FIRST run initializes every cursor to CURRENT END OF FILE and processes nothing — backlogs are never replayed (this exact failure bombarded the owner tonight). Subsequent runs read only appended rows. Atomic writes.
3. CLASSIFY each new escalation row deterministically by issue-text/code patterns into: infra_restartable (unit/timer/service failure, receipt_stale, heartbeat gaps), release_drift (drift/mismatch/pin), auth_needed (SSO, token, login, OAuth, 401), objective_breach (below minimum/setpoint, OBJECTIVE_BELOW_MIN), approval_pending (should not be here — note and skip), unknown. Fingerprint dedupe within and across runs (state/triage/seen_fingerprints.jsonl, resolved-reopen semantics like factory/manager.py's — read it).
4. GOAL AWARENESS: for objective_breach rows, load the department charter and enrich the item with the objective's label/minimum/target so the digest says WHAT GOAL is at risk in the owner's language, not a raw code.
5. ADDRESS-THROUGH-RINGER (propose, never launch): for infra_restartable and release_drift classes, write ONE consolidated proposed Ringer manifest per class per run to <repo-root>/ringer/triage-proposals/<UTCdate>-<class>.json — real manifest shape (run_name 'triage-<class>', tasks with self-contained specs naming the failing units/departments and the diagnosis, checks that verify the service/drift state after fix, engine codex) — plus a matching selfheal proposal card via factory.selfheal.propose_patch for each affected node where its incident shape fits (fix_class 'runtime_config' or 'stale_artifact'; never ALWAYS_HUMAN classes). The agent NEVER executes manifests, never restarts units, never edits code — the coordinator/owner launches proposals. auth_needed and unknown are never proposed as fixes.
6. HUMAN DIGEST: at most max_pings_per_run (default 1) Telegram ping per run, and only when human-class items (auth_needed, objective_breach, unknown) exist: one compact line, e.g. '[triage] 2 need you: AWS SSO expired (sweeper blocked); hopper 0 < min 2. 3 fix proposals queued.' Cooldown: an identical digest fingerprint within digest_cooldown_hours is not re-sent (state/triage/last_digest.json). --execute required for the ping and all state/proposal writes; dry run prints everything it WOULD do.
7. AUDIT: append every decision (row fingerprint, class, action taken: proposed|digested|suppressed_duplicate|skipped) to state/triage/audit.jsonl, fsync'd. Logging module; stdout = one JSON receipt {rows, by_class, proposals_written, pinged}.
8. templates/systemd/loop-factory-triage.{service,timer}: service runs 'python3 -m factory.triage_agent --repo-root {{REPO}} --config %h/.config/loop-factory/triage.yaml --execute'; timer OnCalendar=*:5/30 (offset from other timers), Persistent=false, installed DISABLED with the house header comments (read the existing templates/systemd files and match their discipline).

tests/test_triage_agent.py — at least 12 fixture tests: first run cursors to EOF and processes zero rows (the anti-bombardment property, test it explicitly); appended row after first run IS processed; classification per class (one test each incl. objective_breach charter enrichment with a fixture charter); dedupe suppresses repeat fingerprints across runs; resolved-reopen re-processes; proposals written as valid JSON manifests with self-contained specs and NEVER for auth/unknown; selfheal proposal card created with auto_apply false; digest: single ping max with faked argv capture, contains owner-language goal text, cooldown suppresses identical digest, different digest sends; dry run writes nothing and pings nothing; audit rows for every decision.

VERIFY: 'PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 loopfactory.py check' full suite green. You fail for touching files outside the owned list, fewer than 12 new 'def test_' functions, or the verify command failing.
tasks.verified: escalations now flow to a goal-aware triage agent that queues Ringer fix proposals for the fixable and sends the owner at most one cooldown-guarded digest per cycle — never a bombardment, never an auto-launched fix
